text: Black thinkers took pride in Haiti, where enslaved people rose up under Toussaint Louverture.
More than 90 years ago, Black students from France's colonies met in Paris, at a salon run by the Nardal sisters.
src: Black intellectuals took pride in Haiti for its slave revolution under Toussaint Louverture in the 1790s
In the 1920s and 1930s young Black students and scholars, mainly from France’s colonies and territories, gathered in Paris / Paulette and Jane Nardal ran the salon where the movement took shape

text: There Aimé Césaire, from Martinique, turned nègre, an insulting French word, into a name of pride: Négritude.
He and his friends Senghor and Damas spoke out against colonial rule and racism.
src: Aimé Césaire, poet, playwright and politician from Martinique / Négritude took nègre, a derogatory French word, and made it a name of empowerment
Its founders, Césaire, Senghor and Damas, rejected colonialism, racism and assimilation

text: They said Black people had a history and culture as worthy as anyone else's.
Léopold Sédar Senghor, a poet, later became the first President of Senegal.
src: They insisted that Black people possessed a history and a worthy culture equal to those of others
Léopold Sédar Senghor, poet and later the first President of Senegal

text: In Senegal, painters of the Dakar School turned its ideas into art.
Some writers, such as Wole Soyinka, criticised it, saying that a tiger does not boast of being a tiger.
src: the Dakar School of art in Senegal, founded under the paternalism of President Senghor, gave the philosophy visual form
Soyinka wrote that “a tiger doesn’t proclaim its tigerness; it jumps on its prey.”

text: It inspired movements in the Caribbean, and the idea "black is beautiful" in the United States.
Historians now say the Nardal sisters belong beside its founders, after their part was long overlooked.
src: Créolité and Antillanité in the Caribbean and black is beautiful in the United States
their name belongs beside those of Césaire, Senghor and Damas / were long minimised in its history
